In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diffractive dijets are a unique tool for a study of nuclear partons and the parton saturation regime in nuclei.
diffractive dijets in DIS off nuclei provide a unique opportunity to define nuclear parton distributions in a saturation regime.
the NZ-NSS formalism is a promising tool for a definition of nuclear parton densities in the saturation regime, but the present state of the art is still far from the conclusive status.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NSS-NZ mechanism for diffractively produced hard dijets in DIS is a unique probe of nuclear parton distributions in a saturation regime.
we have found that diffractive hard scattering off nuclei is a unique tool for studying the saturation regime of QCD.
the NSS analysis of diffractively produced dijets is consistent with the definition of nuclear saturation densities in terms of the Golec-Biernat-Wusthoff model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nuclear parton distributions in the saturation regime are not simply a convolution of the proton parton densities with nuclear shadowing.
the saturation scale Qs is a function of the parton transverse momentum.

, in contrast to the standard picture where the saturation momentum is a function of Bjorken x and the nuclear thickness, the saturation momentum is in reality a function of Bj x, the nuclear thickness, and the transverse momentum squared of the parton.
